answer: Agents broadcast a signed, time‑stamped signal containing a hash of their recent interaction graph, creating a spiral of dependencies that leads to a trusted haven of vetted nodes. To join, a newcomer must present a verifiable path through this spiral, paying a fee that grows exponentially with each added link. An attacker must forge distinct paths and pay the cumulative exponential cost, rendering large‑scale Sybil attacks financially infeasible.
